classification.difficultyReason: Find a shorter side, then compare the two path lengths without prematurely rounding.

content.prompt: Two ants take different paths $CA$ and $BA$, respectively, while walking back to their nest at point $A$. How much further does one ant walk than the other? Round your answer to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Horizontal hypotenuse CB extends beyond both vertices; A lies below, with a right-angle mark and an outlined nest circle. Decorative ants are omitted. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: CB = 4 m, CA = 3 m, angle CAB = 90 degrees. Coordinates derive from these givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; BA and the path difference are not supplied.

answer.short: $0.35\text{ m}$; the ant following $CA$ walks further.
answer.worked:
Since $CB$ is opposite the right angle, it is the hypotenuse. By Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}BA^2+3^2&=4^2\\BA^2+9&=16\\BA^2&=16-9\\BA^2&=7\\BA&=\sqrt7\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
The difference in path lengths is
$$\begin{align*}CA-BA&=3-\sqrt7\\CA-BA&\approx0.35\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
The ant following $CA$ walks $0.35\text{ m}$ further, correct to 2 decimal places.
